description: Settle Workflow-owned Agent tasks only from authoritative results: preserve one execution identity across inconclusive physical facts, reconcile replay safely, block after a fixed deadline, and expose actionable non-failure attention.

tasks.title: Make TaskRun settlement the authority for Agent outcomes
tasks.description: Add `AgentResultSettlement` to `TaskRun` as the single arbitration authority for Workflow-owned `mohist/agent`, `mohist/opencode`, and `mohist/pi` attempts. Include identity-fenced bind and observation operations, reportable-attempt lookup for active or unresolved work, and one derived `HasUnresolvedAgentResult` predicate for downstream controls and projections. Keep settlement state out of task and stage status enums, apart from the minimum run-level blocked value later required for indexed queries.
acceptanceCriteria: Every claimed Workflow Agent task has one `AgentResultSettlement` containing its real `TaskRun.Id`, `WorkId`, and assigned Runner; checks and non-Agent tasks create no settlement.
`BindAgentExecutionAsync` accepts an exact replay as a no-op and rejects a Session, Turn, runtime target, task attempt, work, or Runner mismatch without changing Workflow state.

`ObserveAgentExecutionAsync` records idle, completed, stopped, stop-unconfirmed, target-missing, or disconnected as physical facts without appending `TaskCompleted`, `TaskFailed`, `StageFailed`, or `WorkflowRunFailed`.

`HasUnresolvedAgentResult` is the only domain predicate exposed for T-002 control fences and T-007 status projection; no independent persisted awaiting/unknown state is added to `StageRunStatus` or duplicated across the aggregate.
Identity lookup accepts exactly the persisted task-run/work/Runner tuple for active, unknown, and blocked Agent work and returns stale for superseded attempts, another Runner, or another work id.

Domain and Workflow grain tests cover exact duplicate binding/observation, identity mismatch, Session-name reuse, stale observations after a terminal result, and unchanged conclusive failure behavior for non-Agent work.
Relevant Server tests and `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Workflow-owned Agent settlement model, identity-fenced bind/observe commands, reportable-attempt lookup, derived unresolved predicates, and passing state-machine tests.
tasks.notes: Keep arbitration inside `WorkflowRun` JSON state so settlement and Workflow events use the existing transaction. `TaskRun.AgentResultSettlement.State` is authoritative; add only the minimum run-level blocked value later required for indexed queries. Physical stop delivery remains owned by issue #562.

tasks.title: Bound unresolved settlement and make explicit stop safe
tasks.description: Implement the Workflow-owned `agent-result-settlement` reminder with injected time, one durable deadline from a configured five-minute default, and a nonterminal blocked transition that emits no failure outcome. Fence dispatch, retry, rerun, runtime insertion, desired redelivery, and lock release while the settlement is unresolved, while retaining connected Runner capacity accounting. Make explicit Workflow stop the sole abandonment transition by committing cancellation and run stop before idempotently releasing the snapshot, reminder, and stage lock.
acceptanceCriteria: The first unknown observation stores `FirstUnknownAt` and one absolute `DeadlineAt`; reconnect, replay, restart, and later observations never extend or replace that deadline.
Every matching duplicate observation invokes `EnsureReminder` after the state decision, and a commit-success/reminder-registration-failure/retry test proves repair without grain reactivation.

Activation reconciles reminder state; an early tick reschedules from the stored deadline; a due tick atomically records blocked settlement/events and then idempotently unregisters using fake time only. Reminder-removal failure is repaired by tick replay or activation.

Unknown and blocked work cannot be redispatched or replaced by claim, retry, rerun, rerun-from-stage, or runtime task insertion; connected Runner `inFlight`/`awaitingAck` keys still consume capacity without becoming desired redelivery.
The dispatch snapshot is deleted on the first unknown transition, while sequential stage locks remain held through unknown and blocked until a matching result or explicit stop commits.

Explicit stop commits task `Cancelled` plus run `Stopped`, retains the execution identity in history, and writes no task/stage/run failure fields or events; idempotent post-commit cleanup releases snapshot/reminder/locks and all later reports and observations are stale.

Stop replay and grain activation repair snapshot deletion, reminder removal, or lock release interrupted after the stop commit; tests inject failure after each boundary and prove the run remains stopped while cleanup converges.

Tests cover the configured five-minute default, before/after-deadline observations, restart repair, reminder registration/removal failure repair, non-dispatchability, lock retention, late result eligibility after blocking, and explicit stop ordering with injectable time and fakes.
Relevant Server tests and `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Durable fixed-deadline reminder, blocked transition, unresolved control fences, explicit cancellation/stop settlement, and passing fake-time recovery tests.
tasks.notes: Do not poll AgentSession or issue a stop from the Workflow reminder. Issue #562 may redeliver only the existing stop operation after positive reconciliation proves the exact recorded target remains active.

tasks.title: Fence Agent runtime start on durable Server binding
tasks.description: Turn Workflow `session.input` into a replay-idempotent pre-execution fence across Runner, AgentSession, and Workflow. Preserve a stable delivery identity and full execution metadata through `RunnerRoutes`, freeze one `SessionWorkflowExecutionBinding` on the created or reused AgentTurn, and bind that identity to the Workflow settlement before returning the Turn receipt. Gate Agent runtime invocation on that Server receipt and stamp its canonical Turn identity on every later event.
acceptanceCriteria: The turn-opening `session.input` carries a stable delivery id plus WorkflowRun, real TaskRun/work, authenticated Runner context, target AgentSession, runtime, and runtime Session identity through the HTTP command; it does not require a pre-existing AgentTurn id.
Replaying the same input delivery id creates no second Agent input or turn and retries any missing Workflow binding before returning a receipt.

The Server returns a matching `session.input` receipt with the created or reused `AgentTurnId` only after both AgentSession state and Workflow settlement binding are durable; mismatched binding returns no successful receipt.
Every later Workflow runtime event carries the `AgentTurnId` returned by the acknowledged input receipt.

`WorkflowAgentSessionReporter.awaitInput` remains pending after local outbox persistence and starts the runtime only after the matching Server receipt; transport failure, timeout, empty/malformed receipt, or binding rejection leaves the record durable for retry and prevents execution.
Runner restart reloads the same pending input identity and can complete binding without creating replacement Workflow work or a second AgentTurn.

Runner tests cover local-persist success with HTTP pending/failure, receipt acknowledgement, restart replay, and no runtime invocation before acknowledgement; Server specs cover durable input/binding replay and mismatch rejection.
Relevant Runner and Server tests plus `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Stable input delivery identity, durable AgentTurn/Workflow binding handshake, receipt-gated Runner execution, and passing cross-boundary replay tests.
tasks.notes: Local outbox persistence is necessary but is not the execution fence. The fence is the Server receipt issued after both grain-owned bindings are durable. Keep calls one-way from AgentSession to Workflow to avoid a grain cycle.

tasks.title: Deliver physical observations with immutable execution identity
tasks.description: Carry the frozen T-003 execution identity on every Workflow runtime event and observation, and partition Runner persistence and delivery batches by that complete identity rather than mutable Session labels. Replace abandonment call sites with identity-fenced physical observations while preserving issue #562 stop-operation ownership, including same-operation redelivery only after positive reconciliation proves the exact recorded target remains active.
acceptanceCriteria: Every persisted Workflow runtime-event record contains enough immutable execution identity to target one Workflow task attempt and Agent turn without reading the Session's current `work-id` label.
The outbox sequence key includes full execution identity; records for reused Sessions, different work attempts, Turns, Runners, or runtime Sessions cannot enter the same delivery batch.
`sendBatch` validates all records before using an envelope and rejects a mixed batch instead of serializing batch-head metadata for later records.

AgentSession terminal, idle, cancelled, stopped, stop-unconfirmed, missing-target, and recovery paths call `ObserveAgentExecutionAsync`; none calls an abandonment boundary that can fail Workflow work.

Recovery creates no new stop-operation identity and redelivers the recorded operation only when the exact target is positively observed active; idle, completed, missing, replaced, or indeterminate targets leave the result unknown.

Runner tests cover mixed identity batches and restart replay; Server tests cover delayed old-Turn observations after Session reuse, exact-target stop reconciliation, and idempotent duplicate observations.
Relevant Runner and Server tests plus `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Full-identity runtime-event persistence/batching, frozen-Turn observation handoff, #562-compatible stop reconciliation, and passing Session-reuse/replay tests.
tasks.notes: A batch may still contain many streaming deltas, but only for one exact execution identity. Do not redesign physical stop delivery or move its reminder into Workflow.

tasks.title: Preserve unknown Agent results through Runner loss and reconnect
tasks.description: Keep inconclusive outcomes separate from authoritative failure across all Workflow Agent executors, and route their explicit `unknown` result through durable observation handling rather than `TaskReportStatus.Failed`. Make Runner closeout record `runner-disconnected` against the original Agent settlement while preserving conclusive failure for checks and non-Agent work, and reconcile retained events or results on reconnect without replacement dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: All Workflow Agent executor paths use `unknown` for unconfirmed cleanup/result authority and reserve failed for a conclusive Agent result; `TaskReportStatus` remains only succeeded/failed.

`WorkflowItemTranslator` and `WorkflowReportService` route unknown Agent results to `ObserveAgentExecutionAsync` without output/artifact/follow-up side effects and retire the Runner result only after durable acknowledgement.

Runner loss for unresolved Workflow Agent work records the original identity, deadline, and `runner-disconnected` reason without `TaskFailed`; checks and non-Agent tasks still follow their current `runner-lost` failure semantics.

Reconnect replays retained input, events, observations, or authoritative result against the same execution and does not make the unresolved item desired work or create a replacement task attempt/turn.
The five issue failure shapes (unconfirmed stop followed by idle/completed, before or after Runner disconnect, in plan or build) remain nonterminal until result, deadline, or explicit stop.

Runner and Server tests cover each Agent executor, unknown acknowledgement failure/replay, Runner disconnect/reconnect, and regressions for conclusive Agent failure, checks, dispatch rejection, and workspace preparation timeout.
Relevant Runner and Server tests plus `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: End-to-end unknown result semantics, Agent-aware Runner loss/reconnect reconciliation, preserved non-Agent failures, and passing regression tests for the observed incidents.
tasks.notes: Connectivity and Session activity are observations, never authoritative results. Do not add blind retry, replacement execution, or an `Unknown` member to `TaskReportStatus`.

tasks.title: Arbitrate late results before replay-safe side effects
tasks.description: Move authoritative result selection and every report side effect behind the serialized Workflow grain turn so the original task attempt is selected by work identity and authenticated Runner before mutation. Make artifact binding replay-idempotent with uniquely indexed `SourceUploadId`, existing-row return on replay, and real TaskRun attribution. Accept the first matching result before or after blocking, and acknowledge every later report as side-effect-free stale.
acceptanceCriteria: No artifact bind, follow-up projection, output/error mutation, Workflow event, or advancement occurs before the Workflow grain has selected an eligible active/unknown/blocked task attempt as the winner.
A matching success before or after blocked completes the original TaskRun and resumes normal advancement once; a matching conclusive failure uses normal task/stage/run failure semantics once.

Every later report for the terminal work identity returns `Stale` and performs no artifact, follow-up, output, event, or advancement side effect, regardless of whether its content matches or conflicts.

An EF migration adds nullable `WorkflowArtifactRow.SourceUploadId` with a unique filtered index for non-null values; every new binding writes it, while historical rows may remain null because their consumed upload identity is unavailable.
Replay looks up `SourceUploadId`, returns the already-bound artifact, consumes no second pending upload, and records `TaskRun.Id` rather than `WorkId`.

A grain-save failure after artifact binding can replay the same upload/result without duplicate artifacts; foreign upload ids and mismatched Runner/work/task identities are rejected before side effects.

Tests cover concurrent/replayed success and failure, late result before and after blocked, stale reports after explicit stop, invalid follow-up/output, artifact bind replay after simulated save failure, and exact TaskRun attribution using fakes/in-memory storage only.
Relevant Server tests and `npm run test:fast` pass.
tasks.output: Serialized late-result arbitration, replay-idempotent artifact binding with real TaskRun attribution, side-effect-free stale acknowledgements, and passing result-replay tests.
tasks.notes: Artifact storage is outside the WorkflowRun transaction, so persisted `SourceUploadId` replay identity is mandatory for every new binding. Do not add a result fingerprint solely to distinguish duplicate from conflicting terminal reports; both are stale by contract.

tasks.title: Project blocked settlement as actionable non-failure attention
tasks.description: Publish first-unknown and blocked Workflow events and expose the authoritative settlement through Server read models with stable reason `agent-result-unconfirmed`, deadline, execution references, and next action. Derive blocked task, stage, and run views from settlement state and project nonterminal attention to Issue, Inbox, Web, and CLI. Keep blocked out of failure fields, failed-task retry controls, terminal polling, and failure-only GitHub, Hermes, and Agent subscribers.
acceptanceCriteria: `AgentTaskResultUnconfirmed`, `TaskBlocked`, `StageBlocked`, and `WorkflowRunBlocked` serialize, persist, query, and map through the event catalog/lineage exactly once without reusing any failed event type.

Task, stage, run, and Issue read models consistently return wire status `running` during unknown and `blocked` after expiry, derived from the authoritative settlement; indexed blocked run queries return the same runs.

Blocked API payloads expose `agent-result-unconfirmed`, actionable message, fixed deadline, original work/Session/Turn references when available, and recovery actions without populating task/stage/run failure fields.

Issue and Inbox show blocked attention; Web status unions, headers, stage icons, task rows, logs, and browser views render blocked; CLI view/list/log output renders blocked and does not terminate run waiting solely because it is blocked.
Blocked events do not reach failure-only GitHub, Hermes, or Agent subscribers and do not offer failed-task retry; explicit stop remains available as the operator escape hatch.
Server event/projection specs, CLI tests, Web unit tests, and browser tests cover unknown-to-blocked-to-late-result and unknown-to-explicit-stop without any failed presentation.
`npm run test:fast` and the full `npm run verify` gate pass.
tasks.output: Blocked Workflow events, indexed/read projections, actionable API contract, Issue/Inbox/Web/CLI presentation, subscriber fencing, and passing full repository verification.
tasks.notes: Blocked is visible and nonterminal. Notification scope is resolved: Issue, Inbox, Web, and CLI receive attention; GitHub, Hermes, and Agent failure subscribers do not. This final coordinated client slice owns `npm run verify`.
